```html
<div id="propagate-a-keplerian-orbit" class="section level2">
<h2>Propagate a Keplerian orbit</h2>
<p>One of Kepler’s laws states that an orbiting object sweeps out equal areas in equal amounts of time. What this law means is that an orbiting object accelerates as it approaches the periapsis and decelerates as it approaches apoapsis. This changinge rate is reflected in Kepler’s equation, E(t) - esin(E) = M(t), which states that the Mean anomaly at time is equal to the Eccentric anomaly at time t minus the eccentricity multiplied by the sine of the Eccentric anomaly. This equation is transcendental because it transcends the simple equations; it must be solved iteratively. Marc Murison developed a practical method for solving Kepler’s equation using a Taylor series expanded to the third order. The following chunk of R code implements Murison’s algorithm.</p>
<p>After the implementation of the algorithm, a function named propagate calls the Keplerian equation solver to generate the True anomaly, which is the current position of an object in an orbit. Code at the end of the chunk uses the propagate function to populate an array of vertices and then implements a playwidget for an interactive 3D model of an orbiting object.</p>
<pre class="r"><code>KeplerStart3 &lt;- function(e,M) {
t34 &lt;- e^2
t35 &lt;- e * t34
t33 &lt;- cos(M)

result &lt;- M+(-1/2*t35+e+(t34+3/2 * t33*t35)*t33)*sin(M)
return(result)
}

eps1 &lt;- function(e,M,x) {
 result &lt;- (x - e * sin(x) - M)/(1 - e * cos(x))
 return(result)
}

eps2 &lt;- function(e,M,x) {
  t1 &lt;- -1 + e * cos(x)
  t2 &lt;- e * sin(x)
  t3 &lt;- -x + t2 + M
  result &lt;- t3/(1/2 *t3 * t2/t1 + t1)
  return(result)
}

eps3 &lt;- function(e,M,x) {
   t1 &lt;- cos(x)
   t2 &lt;- -1 + e * t1
   t3 &lt;- sin(x)
   t4 &lt;- e*t3
   t5 &lt;- -x + t4 + M
   t6 &lt;- t5/(1/2 * t5 * t4/t2 + t2)
   result &lt;- t5/((1/2 * t3 - 1/6 * t1 * t6) * e * t6 + t2)
   return(result)
}

KeplerSolve &lt;- function(e, M) {
   tol &lt;- 1.0e-14
   Mnorm &lt;- M %% 2 * pi
   E0 &lt;- KeplerStart3(e, Mnorm)
   dE &lt;- tol + 1
   count &lt;- 0

   while (dE &gt; tol) {
      E &lt;- E0 - eps3(e, Mnorm, E0)
      dE &lt;- abs(E - E0)
      E0 &lt;- E
      count &lt;- count + 1
      
      if (count == 100) {
         msg &lt;- &quot;Astounding! KeplerSolve failed to converge!&quot;
         print(msg)
         break
      } #endif
   } # end while

   return(E)
}

 propagate &lt;- function(clock) {
  T &lt;- 120      # seconds
  n &lt;- 2*pi/T
  tau &lt;- 0      # time of pericenter passage

  M &lt;- n * (clock - tau)
  E &lt;- KeplerSolve(e,M)
  cose &lt;- cos(E) # shows up multiple times so calculate once.

  r = a*(1 - e * cose)
  s.x &lt;- r * ((cose - e)/(1 - e * cose))
  s.y &lt;- r * ((sqrt(1 - e^2)*sin(E))/(1 - e * cose))
  s.z &lt;- 0
  
  point &lt;- rotate3d(c(s.x,s.y,s.z),pi/5,0,1,0)
  point &lt;- rotate3d(c(point[1],point[2],point[3]),pi/4,0,0,1)
  point &lt;- rotate3d(c(point[1],point[2],point[3]),pi/4,1,0,0)

  return(point)
 }
 
par3d(zoom=0.8)     # set a parameter
orbit &lt;- plot3d(x.raan,y.raan,z.raan,type=&quot;l&quot;, col=&quot;black&quot;)
spheres3d(0,0,0,radius=0.2, col=&quot;blue&quot;)

ts &lt;- 120  # Number of time slices.
orbcoords &lt;- cbind(1:ts,0,0) # Allocate a three column array.
for (clock in 1:ts) {
 loc &lt;- propagate(clock)
 orbcoords[clock,1] &lt;- loc[1]
 orbcoords[clock,2] &lt;- loc[2]  # Populate the array of vertices.
 orbcoords[clock,3] &lt;- loc[3]
}
# Put a small sphere in the orbit.
 sphereid &lt;- spheres3d(xyz.coords(x=loc[1],y=loc[2],z=loc[3]), 
             radius = 0.04, col = &quot;green&quot;)
 
clock &lt;- 1:ts
rglwidget() %&gt;%
  playwidget(list(
  ageControl(births = 1, ages = clock, vertices = orbcoords, objids = sphereid)),
  start = 1, stop = max(clock), rate = 5,
  components = c(&quot;Reverse&quot;, &quot;Play&quot;, &quot;Slower&quot;, &quot;Faster&quot;,
                 &quot;Reset&quot;, &quot;Slider&quot;, &quot;Label&quot;),
  loop = TRUE)</code></pre>
```

```html
<div class="fluid-row" id="header">



<h1 class="title toc-ignore">Elliptical Orbit Simulator</h1>
<h4 class="author"><em>Daniel A. O’Neil</em></h4>
<h4 class="date"><em>April 14, 2017</em></h4>

</div>


<div id="introduction" class="section level2">
<h2>Introduction</h2>
<p>The R programming language can produce Web-based Space Mission Visualizations (WSMV). With the rgl package, a space mission designer can create interactive animated 3D scenes and export JavaScript and WebGL. With the R Markdown language, a WSMV developer can design documents and with the RPubs service provided by the makers of RStudio, the WSMV can be published online.</p>
</div>
<div id="scope" class="section level2">
<h2>Scope</h2>
<p>The Physics department in College of Saint Benedict+Saint John’s University explains the geometry for 2D and 3D Orbits and provides example Mathematica code. Essentially, those web-pages describe a procedure of specifying a 2D ellipse and then applying 3D rotations to the ellipse using the Keplarian parameters. To gain some insight to the 2D geometry, visit <a href="http://www.physics.csbsju.edu/orbit/orbit.2d.html" class="uri">http://www.physics.csbsju.edu/orbit/orbit.2d.html</a>.then click on the link to the 3D orbit web-page.<a href="http://www.physics.csbsju.edu/orbit/orbit.3d.html" class="uri">http://www.physics.csbsju.edu/orbit/orbit.3d.html</a> This tutorial applies the methodology of specifying a 2D ellipse and then applying pitch, yaw, and roll rotation matrices to orient the ellipse in three dimensions. The following image depicts these transformations.</p>
</div>
<div id="generate-a-flat-surface-ellipse" class="section level2">
<h2>Generate a flat surface ellipse</h2>
<p>Generating an ellipse involves setting a value for a semi-major axis, <em>a</em>, and eccentricity, <em>e</em>. With an <em>e = 0</em>, the ellipse would be a circle; with an <em>e = 1</em>, the ellipses becomes a line. A value between zero and one gives an ellipse a shape somewhere between a circle and a line. The following chunk of R code generates an ellipse.</p>
<pre class="r"><code>#Initialize
a &lt;- 1                  # semi-major axis
e &lt;- 1/sqrt(2)          # eccentricity
b &lt;- a * sqrt(1 - e^2)  # semi-minor axis
c &lt;- e * a              # distance from the center to a focus

# Distance from a focus to the center.
x.c &lt;- -c
y.c &lt;- 0
z.c &lt;- 0

# Generate a numerical sequence
u &lt;- seq(-pi,pi, length.out=80)

# Generate x and y values.
x &lt;- a * cos(u) - e
y &lt;- a * sqrt(1-e^2) * sin(u)
z &lt;- rep(0, times=80)

c.x &lt;- a * cos(u) - c
c.y &lt;- a * sin(u)         # Generate points for an outer circle.
c.z &lt;- rep(0, times=80)

# Plot x &amp; y with a line.
plot(x,y,type=&quot;l&quot;, ylim=c(-a*sin(pi/2), a*sin(pi/2)),asp=1)
points(c.x,c.y,type=&quot;l&quot;, col=&quot;green&quot;)</code></pre>
<p><img src="data:image/png;base64," width="672" /></p>
</div>
<div id="transform-the-flat-ellipse-into-a-3d-orbit" class="section level2">
<h2>Transform the flat ellipse into a 3D orbit</h2>
<p>Install the R package named rgl. Documentation for rgl is available at <a href="https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rgl/vignettes/rgl.html" class="uri">https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rgl/vignettes/rgl.html</a>. The following R code performs three rotations. Think of an orbit as an airplane. A plane can pitch up or down, it can yaw, i.e., rotate around its vertical axis, and it can roll. In addition to the semi-major axis and eccentricity, other Keplarian parameters include inclination, longitude of the ascending node, ??, and the Right Ascension of the Ascending Node (RAAN). Using inclination for pitch, ?? for yaw, and RAAN for roll, we can rotate the flat ellipse around the X, Y, and Z axes. The following R code initializes three arrays, x.inc, y.inc, z.inc, to hold the values for the inclined ellipse. A for loop steps through each of the values stored in the x, y, z values and applies a 3D rotation matrix. Parameters of the rotate3d function include the object, the angle, and the axis. In this case, the object is one of the Cartesian coordinates, an angle of pi/5, and the 0, 1, 0 represents the Y axis. After calculating the new point, the x, y, and z values are stored in the x.inc, y.inc, and z.inc arrays. The rest of the code on this page conducts similar transformations for yaw, i.e. ??, and roll, i.e. RAAN.</p>
<pre class="r"><code># Pitch ~ inclination, tilt about the y axis.
x.inc &lt;- rep(0, times=80)
y.inc &lt;- rep(0, times=80)
z.inc &lt;- rep(0, times=80)

for (i in 1:80) {
 point &lt;- rotate3d(c(x[i],y[i],z[i]),pi/5,0,1,0)
 x.inc[i] &lt;- point[1]
 y.inc[i] &lt;- point[2]
 z.inc[i] &lt;- point[3]
}
# Transform the focus for the central body.
center &lt;- rotate3d(c(x.c,y.c,z.c),pi/5,0,1,0)

# Yaw ~ longitude of the ascending node (omega),
# so rotate around the z axis.
x.om &lt;- rep(0, times=80)
y.om &lt;- rep(0, times=80)
z.om &lt;- rep(0, times=80)

for (i in 1:80) {
 point &lt;- rotate3d(c(x.inc[i],y.inc[i],z.inc[i]),pi/4,0,0,1)
 x.om[i] &lt;- point[1]
 y.om[i] &lt;- point[2]
 z.om[i] &lt;- point[3]
}
# Transform the focus for the central body.
center &lt;- rotate3d(c(center[1],center[2],center[3]),pi/4,0,0,1)

# Roll ~ Right ascension of the ascending node (RAAN),
# so rotate around the x axis.
x.raan &lt;- rep(0, times=80)
y.raan &lt;- rep(0, times=80)
z.raan &lt;- rep(0, times=80)

for (i in 1:80) {
 point &lt;- rotate3d(c(x.om[i],y.om[i],z.om[i]),pi/4,1,0,0)
 x.raan [i] &lt;- point[1]
 y.raan [i] &lt;- point[2]
 z.raan [i] &lt;- point[3]
}
# Transform the focus for the central body.
center &lt;- rotate3d(c(center[1],center[2],center[3]),pi/4,1,0,0)</code></pre>
</div>
<div id="plot-the-transformed-ellipses" class="section level2">
<h2>Plot the transformed ellipses</h2>
<p>Each of transformations stored the values in new variables. The following code sets parameters for a 3D device, establishes layout of one row with three columns, and plots interactive image of the transformed ellipses. The rglwidget function embeds the interactive plot within a web-page.</p>
<p><em>You can click-drag to rotate and right-click-drag to zoom in and out the following 3D plots</em>.</p>
<pre class="r"><code># Plot the transformed elliptical orbit.
par3d(zoom=0.8, windowRect = c(200, 5, 800, 400))
mfrow3d(nr = 1, nc = 3, sharedMouse = TRUE) 

plot3d(x=x.inc,y=y.inc,z=z.inc, type=&quot;l&quot;, col=&quot;red&quot;)
next3d()
plot3d(x=x.om,y=y.om,z=z.om, type=&quot;l&quot;, col=&quot;blue&quot;)
next3d()
plot3d(x=x.raan ,y=y.raan ,z=z.raan, type=&quot;l&quot;, col=&quot;green&quot;)
rglwidget()</code></pre>
<div class="figure" style="text-align: center">

<div id="propagate-a-keplerian-orbit" class="section level2">
<h2>Propagate a Keplerian orbit</h2>
<p>One of Kepler’s laws states that an orbiting object sweeps out equal areas in equal amounts of time. What this law means is that an orbiting object accelerates as it approaches the periapsis and decelerates as it approaches apoapsis. This changinge rate is reflected in Kepler’s equation, E(t) - esin(E) = M(t), which states that the Mean anomaly at time is equal to the Eccentric anomaly at time t minus the eccentricity multiplied by the sine of the Eccentric anomaly. This equation is transcendental because it transcends the simple equations; it must be solved iteratively. Marc Murison developed a practical method for solving Kepler’s equation using a Taylor series expanded to the third order. The following chunk of R code implements Murison’s algorithm.</p>
<p>After the implementation of the algorithm, a function named propagate calls the Keplerian equation solver to generate the True anomaly, which is the current position of an object in an orbit. Code at the end of the chunk uses the propagate function to populate an array of vertices and then implements a playwidget for an interactive 3D model of an orbiting object.</p>
<pre class="r"><code>KeplerStart3 &lt;- function(e,M) {
t34 &lt;- e^2
t35 &lt;- e * t34
t33 &lt;- cos(M)

result &lt;- M+(-1/2*t35+e+(t34+3/2 * t33*t35)*t33)*sin(M)
return(result)
}

eps1 &lt;- function(e,M,x) {
 result &lt;- (x - e * sin(x) - M)/(1 - e * cos(x))
 return(result)
}

eps2 &lt;- function(e,M,x) {
  t1 &lt;- -1 + e * cos(x)
  t2 &lt;- e * sin(x)
  t3 &lt;- -x + t2 + M
  result &lt;- t3/(1/2 *t3 * t2/t1 + t1)
  return(result)
}

eps3 &lt;- function(e,M,x) {
   t1 &lt;- cos(x)
   t2 &lt;- -1 + e * t1
   t3 &lt;- sin(x)
   t4 &lt;- e*t3
   t5 &lt;- -x + t4 + M
   t6 &lt;- t5/(1/2 * t5 * t4/t2 + t2)
   result &lt;- t5/((1/2 * t3 - 1/6 * t1 * t6) * e * t6 + t2)
   return(result)
}

KeplerSolve &lt;- function(e, M) {
   tol &lt;- 1.0e-14
   Mnorm &lt;- M %% 2 * pi
   E0 &lt;- KeplerStart3(e, Mnorm)
   dE &lt;- tol + 1
   count &lt;- 0

   while (dE &gt; tol) {
      E &lt;- E0 - eps3(e, Mnorm, E0)
      dE &lt;- abs(E - E0)
      E0 &lt;- E
      count &lt;- count + 1
      
      if (count == 100) {
         msg &lt;- &quot;Astounding! KeplerSolve failed to converge!&quot;
         print(msg)
         break
      } #endif
   } # end while

   return(E)
}

 propagate &lt;- function(clock) {
  T &lt;- 120      # seconds
  n &lt;- 2*pi/T
  tau &lt;- 0      # time of pericenter passage

  M &lt;- n * (clock - tau)
  E &lt;- KeplerSolve(e,M)
  cose &lt;- cos(E) # shows up multiple times so calculate once.

  r = a*(1 - e * cose)
  s.x &lt;- r * ((cose - e)/(1 - e * cose))
  s.y &lt;- r * ((sqrt(1 - e^2)*sin(E))/(1 - e * cose))
  s.z &lt;- 0
  
  point &lt;- rotate3d(c(s.x,s.y,s.z),pi/5,0,1,0)
  point &lt;- rotate3d(c(point[1],point[2],point[3]),pi/4,0,0,1)
  point &lt;- rotate3d(c(point[1],point[2],point[3]),pi/4,1,0,0)

  return(point)
 }
 
par3d(zoom=0.8)     # set a parameter
orbit &lt;- plot3d(x.raan,y.raan,z.raan,type=&quot;l&quot;, col=&quot;black&quot;)
spheres3d(0,0,0,radius=0.2, col=&quot;blue&quot;)

ts &lt;- 120  # Number of time slices.
orbcoords &lt;- cbind(1:ts,0,0) # Allocate a three column array.
for (clock in 1:ts) {
 loc &lt;- propagate(clock)
 orbcoords[clock,1] &lt;- loc[1]
 orbcoords[clock,2] &lt;- loc[2]  # Populate the array of vertices.
 orbcoords[clock,3] &lt;- loc[3]
}
# Put a small sphere in the orbit.
 sphereid &lt;- spheres3d(xyz.coords(x=loc[1],y=loc[2],z=loc[3]), 
             radius = 0.04, col = &quot;green&quot;)
 
clock &lt;- 1:ts
rglwidget() %&gt;%
  playwidget(list(
  ageControl(births = 1, ages = clock, vertices = orbcoords, objids = sphereid)),
  start = 1, stop = max(clock), rate = 5,
  components = c(&quot;Reverse&quot;, &quot;Play&quot;, &quot;Slower&quot;, &quot;Faster&quot;,
                 &quot;Reset&quot;, &quot;Slider&quot;, &quot;Label&quot;),
  loop = TRUE)</code></pre>
```

```
[ {
  "@id" : "http://example.org/demo#Orbit",
  "@type" : [ "http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#Class" ],
  "http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment" : [ {
    "@value" : "An orbit describes the trajectory of an object moving around another object.  Typically, the shape of orbits range from circular to elliptical.  Hyperbolic orbits are objects moving past another object."
  } ],
  "http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#label" : [ {
    "@language" : "en",
    "@value" : "Orbit"
  } ]
}, {
  "@id" : "http://example.org/demo#eccentricity",
  "@type" : [ "http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#DatatypeProperty" ],
  "http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment" : [ {
    "@value" : "Eccentricity describes the shape of the ellipse; it's the distance from the center to one of the foci.  As the eccentricity value approaches one the ellipse squashes and becomes elongated.  As the eccentricity value approaches zero, the ellipse becomes a circle."
  } ]
}, {
  "@id" : "http://example.org/demo#inclination",
  "@type" : [ "http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#DatatypeProperty" ],
  "http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment" : [ {
    "@value" : "Inclination is the angle between a plane that runs through the equator of the object being orbited and the trajectory of the orbiting object.  If the orbit is above the main object's equator then the inclination is zero.   The inclination can range from zero to 180 degrees."
  } ]
}, {
  "@id" : "http://example.org/demo#omega",
  "@type" : [ "http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#DatatypeProperty" ],
  "http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment" : [ {
    "@value" : "Ascending node -- a line is defined by the intersection of the plane defined by the equator of the main object and the plane defined by the orbital trajectory.  The end points of the line are the ascending and descending node.  Omega represents the ascending node where the orbiting object is rising through the equatorial plane."
  } ]
}, {
  "@id" : "http://example.org/demo#period",
  "@type" : [ "http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#DatatypeProperty" ],
  "http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment" : [ {
    "@value" : "Period is the amount of time that it takes for an orbiting object to complete a revolution of the trajectory."
  } ]
}, {
  "@id" : "http://example.org/demo#sma",
  "@type" : [ "http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#DatatypeProperty" ],
  "http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment" : [ {
    "@value" : "Semi major axis is one half of the major axis, which is the longest line that stretches across an ellipse."
  } ]
}, {
  "@id" : "http://example.org/demo#tau",

  "http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment" : [ {
    "@value" : "Argument of perihelion is the distance from the center of the Sun to the orbiting planet's ascending node."
  } ]
}, {

    "@value" : "The Orbit class is just one of many classes in the Space Situational Awareness Ontology (SSAO) created by Robert Rovetto.  For the purpose of the tutorials and orrery demonstration, the authors have provided this single class ontology populated with values for the Keplerian parameters that describe the orbits of the planets in our solar system.  Additional information about the SSAO is available at \nhttp://rrovetto.github.io/space-situational-awareness-domain-ontology/. var dat = new Blob();          // a blob to hold the content of the uploaded file
```
```html
var rec = {} ;				   // a record for date, time, and Cartesian coordinates
var records = new Array() ;    // an array of records  <-- Presently, not used.
var recCount = 0 ;             // a counter for the records in the array
var curPos = 0 ;               // current position within the current line of text
var curChar = "" ;             // current character within the current line of text
var curEOL = 0 ;               // calculated End Of Line using curPos + linewidth
var lineWidth = 0;             // number of characters in the line of text
var totalChar = 0 ;            // Calculated number of characters in the file

function extractData(someText) {
    var theData = "" ;
	var currentPosition = 0 ;
	var maxChar = someText.length ;

   while (theData == "") {
    if (someText[currentPosition] == " ") {
	// Find the next non-blank character.
	   while (someText[currentPosition] == " ") {
			  currentPosition = currentPosition + 1 ;   
		} // end while
	}   // end if
    else {
	// Update the global current position.
	   curPos = curPos + currentPosition ;              
	   while (someText[currentPosition] != " ") {
	         theData = theData + someText[currentPosition] ;
			 currentPosition = currentPosition + 1 ;
		} // end while
	  } // end else
    } // end while
	
	return theData ;
} // end extractData

  function handleFile() {
		var fileInput = document.getElementById('fileInput');
		var fileDisplayArea = document.getElementById('fileDisplayArea');

		fileInput.addEventListener('change', function(e) {
			var file = fileInput.files[0];
			totalChar = file.size;          // Get the total number of characters.
			var textType = /text.*/;
			if (file.type.match(textType)) {
				var reader = new FileReader();

				reader.onload = function(e) {
				 	dat = reader.result;    // Get the contents of the file.
					curChar = dat[0] ;      // Start at the first character
					while (curChar != "\n") {        // Find the end of line.
					    lineWidth = lineWidth + 1 ;  // Count characters in line.
						curChar = dat[lineWidth] ;
					}	
					curPos = lineWidth + 1;          // Advance to the next line.					
					
					var iNumLines = dat.length/lineWidth ;

					fileDisplayArea.textContent = '{"coordinates":[ \n' ;
				for (var i = 0; i < iNumLines; i++) { 

					curEOL = curPos + lineWidth ;
					
			        rec.date = dat.slice(curPos, curPos+12);
					curPos = curPos + 12;
					rec.time = dat.slice(curPos, curPos+12);
					
					curPos = curPos + 12 ;
					
				if (curPos < totalChar) {  // Have we reached end of the file?
					rec.X = "" ;
					rec.X = extractData(dat.slice(curPos, curEOL)) ;
					curPos = curPos + rec.X.length + 1 ;
					
					rec.Y = "" ;
					rec.Y = extractData(dat.slice(curPos, curEOL)) ;
					curPos = curPos + rec.Y.length + 1;
					
					rec.Z = "" ;
					rec.Z = extractData(dat.slice(curPos, curEOL)) ;			    
				
					recCount = recCount + 1;                                     // not used
					fileDisplayArea.textContent = fileDisplayArea.textContent +
											   "{" + '"Date":' + '"' + rec.date + '"' + "," 
				                                   + '"Time":' + '"' + rec.time + '"' + ","
												   + '"X":' + rec.X + ","
												   + '"Y":' + rec.Y +  ","
												   + '"Z":' + rec.Z  ; 
					fileDisplayArea.textContent = fileDisplayArea.textContent  + "}, \n";
				} // end if
				  
				   curPos = curEOL + 1 ;
				} // next
				var sTraJSON = fileDisplayArea.textContent.toString() ;
				var iLastCharNum = sTraJSON.length ;
				
				sTraJSON = sTraJSON.substring(0,iLastCharNum -3) ;
				sTraJSON = sTraJSON + "]}" ;
				
				fileDisplayArea.textContent = sTraJSON ;
			} 
				 reader.readAsText(file) ; 

			} else {
				fileDisplayArea.innerText = "File not supported!"
			}
		});	
  }
</script>
```

```html
// Constructor to generate objects that identify orbital elements.
function Trajectory(name, smA,oI,aP,oE,aN,mAe,Sidereal){

   this.name = name                          // name the object
   this.smA = smA                            // semi major axis
   this.oI = oI * 0.01745329                 // orbital inclination --> convert degrees to radians
   this.aP = aP * 0.01745329                 // argument of Perigee --> convert degrees to radians
   this.oE = oE                              // orbital eccentricity
   this.aN = aN * 0.01745329                 // ascending node --> convert degrees to radians
   this.period = Sidereal                    // siderial period as a multiple of Earth's orbital period
   this.epochMeanAnomaly = mAe * 0.01745329  // mean anomaly at epoch 
   this.trueAnomoly = 0                      // initialize to mean anomaly at epoch
   this.position = [0,0,0] 
   this.time = 0 
}
//--------------------------------------------
//        Trajectory Propagator
//--------------------------------------------
Trajectory.prototype.propagate = function(uA){
// Purpose: Determine a position on an orbital trajectory based on a true anomoly.
// Used by the traceOrbits function to draw the orbits.
var pos = [] ;
var xdot; var ydot; var zdot;       // velocity coordinates
var theta = uA;                     // Update true anomaly.
var smA = this.smA;                 // Semi-major Axis
var oI =  this.oI ;                 // Orbital Inclination
var aP = this.aP ;                  // Get the object's orbital elements.
var oE = this.oE;                   // Orbital eccentricity
var aN = this.aN ;                  // ascending Node
var sLR = smA * (1 - oE^2) ;             // Compute Semi-Latus Rectum.
var r = sLR/(1 + oE * Math.cos(theta));  // Compute radial distance.

// Compute position coordinates pos[0] is x, pos[1] is y, pos[2] is z
pos[0] = r * (Math.cos(aP + theta) * Math.cos(aN) - Math.cos(oI) * Math.sin(aP + theta) * Math.sin(aN)) ;  
pos[1] = r * (Math.cos(aP + theta) * Math.sin(aN) + Math.cos(oI) * Math.sin(aP + theta) * Math.cos(aN)) ;
pos[2] = r * (Math.sin(aP + theta) * Math.sin(oI)) ;

return pos ;
}

function addNode(identifier,cR,cG,cB,radius)
    { // Create a shape and append it to the transform associated with the Sun.
	    var x = 0; var y = 0; var z = -5; 
        var t = document.createElement('Transform');
        t.setAttribute("translation", x + " " + y + " " + z );
        t.setAttribute("id", identifier);
		
        var s = document.createElement('Shape');          // Shape node
		var app = document.createElement('Appearance');   // Appearance Node
		var mat = document.createElement('Material');	  // Material Node
		    mat.setAttribute("id", identifier + 'Mat');
            mat.setAttribute("diffuseColor", cR + " " + cG + " " + cB );

		app.appendChild(mat);
		s.appendChild(app);
        t.appendChild(s);

        var b = document.createElement('Sphere');
        b.setAttribute("radius", radius);

        s.appendChild(b);
        var ot = document.getElementById('theSun');
        ot.appendChild(t);
      
       return false;
    };

function addLabel(identifier) 
{ // Create a text label and display it above the identified shape.

		var tC = ot.getAttribute("translation") ;
		
		var t = document.createElement('Transform');
		// Translate up and forward for the label.
        t.setAttribute("translation", tC[0] + " " + tC[1] - 0.1 + " " + tC[2] - 0.1);
        t.setAttribute("id", identifier + "Label");

		txt.appendChild(fs);

        ot.appendChild(t);
}
/*-------------------------------------------------------------*
 *   Utility functions for true, eccentric and mean anomalies  *
 *-------------------------------------------------------------*/
 function trueToEccentricAnomaly(e,f) {
// http://mmae.iit.edu/~mpeet/Classes/MMAE441/Spacecraft/441Lecture19.pdf slide 7 
 var eccentricAnomaly = 2* Math.atan(Math.sqrt((1-e)/(1+e))* Math.tan(f/2));

	return eccentricAnomaly ;
}
function meanToEccentricAnomaly (e, M) {
// Solves for eccentric anomaly, E from a given mean anomaly, M
// and eccentricty, e.  Performs a simple Newton-Raphson iteration
// Code derived from Matlab scripts written by Richard Rieber, 1/23/2005
// http://www.mathworks.com/matlabcentral/fileexchange/6779-calce-m
   var tol = 0.0001;  // tolerance
   var eAo = M;       // initialize eccentric anomaly with mean anomaly
   var ratio = 1;     // set ratio higher than the tolerance
while (Math.abs(ratio) > tol) {
    var f_E = eAo - e * Math.sin(eAo) - M;
    var f_Eprime = 1 - e * Math.cos(eAo);
    ratio = f_E / f_Eprime;
    if (Math.abs(ratio) > tol) {
        eAo = eAo - ratio;
	 // console.log ("ratio  " + ratio) ;
	  }
    else
        eccentricAnomaly = eAo;
   }
    return eccentricAnomaly 
} 
function eccentricToTrueAnomaly(e, E) {
 // http://mmae.iit.edu/~mpeet/Classes/MMAE441/Spacecraft/441Lecture19.pdf slide 8
	var trueAnomaly = 2 * Math.atan(Math.sqrt((1+e)/(1-e))* Math.tan(E/2));
	return trueAnomaly
}
/*
function meanToEccentricAnomaly(ec,m) {
    // Source: http://www.jgiesen.de/kepler/kepler.html
    // arguments:
    // ec=eccentricity, m=mean anomaly,
    // dp=number of decimal places
	var dp =  5 ;

    var pi = Math.PI, K = Math.PI/180.0;
    var maxIter=30, i=0;
    var delta = Math.pow(10,-dp);

    var E, F;
    m= m / 360.0;
    m=2.0*pi*(m-Math.floor(m));
    if (ec < 0.8) E=m; else E=pi;
    F = E - ec * Math.sin(m) - m;

    while ((Math.abs(F) > delta) && (i<maxIter)) {
        E = E - F/(1.0- ec* Math.cos(E));
        F = E - ec * Math.sin(E) - m;
        i = i + 1;
    }
    E=E/K;
    return Math.round(E*Math.pow(10,dp))/Math.pow(10,dp);
} */
/*-------------------------------------------------*
 *        Animate the X3D objects                  *
 *-------------------------------------------------*/
function updatePosition() 
	{  // With each tick of the clock, propagate the position and set the translation attribute.
	  // Update the position for the following array of objects.
	  var currentPosition = [] ;
      var deltaTime = 0 ;
	  for (var hB in heavenlyBodies) {
	    
		var hbTAnomoly = heavenlyBodies[hB].trueAnomoly ;
	    currentPosition = heavenlyBodies[hB].propagate(hbTAnomoly) ;  // Determine the current position.
		
	    var Xpos = currentPosition[0] ;
	    var Ypos = currentPosition[1] ;
	    var Zpos = currentPosition[2] ;
		var hBName = heavenlyBodies[hB].name ;   // get the name of the current object and update translation
	    document.getElementById(hBName).setAttribute('translation',Xpos + " " + Ypos + " " + Zpos );
		  
	 // Calculate mean motion n:
		 var n = (2 * Math.PI) / (heavenlyBodies[hB].period * 365.25) ;   // radians per day
		 
	 // Calculate Eccentric Anomaly E based on the orbital eccentricity and previous true anomaly:
	    var e = heavenlyBodies[hB].oE ;
		var f = heavenlyBodies[hB].trueAnomoly          // heavenlyBodies[hB].trueAnomoly ;
        var eA = trueToEccentricAnomaly(e,f)            // convert from true anomaly to eccentric anomaly
		
	 // Calculate current Mean Anomaly	
		var m0 = eA - e * Math.sin(eA);	
	   
	 // deltaTime = (Math.abs(m0/n) - heavenlyBodies[hB].time) * simSpeed
    //  deltaTime = Math.abs(m0/n) * simSpeed
	    deltaTime = simSpeed * n

	 // Update Mean anomaly by adding the Mean Anomaly at Epoch to the mean motion * delaTime
         var mA = deltaTime + m0
	    // var mA = n + m0
		
		heavenlyBodies[hB].time = heavenlyBodies[hB].time +  deltaTime // increment timer
		// heavenlyBodies[hB].time = heavenlyBodies[hB].time +  n // increment timer
		
	//	console.log(hBName + " time = " +  heavenlyBodies[hB].time + "  delta time " + dt)
	//	if (mA >  2 * Math.PI) {
		   // This heavenly body has completed an orbital period so subtract 2*Pi
	//	   mA = mA - 2 * Math.PI
	//	   heavenlyBodies[hB].time = heavenlyBodies[hB].epochMeanAnomaly / n  // reset to tau
		  // heavenlyBodies[hB].time = n
	//	}  

        eA = meanToEccentricAnomaly (e, mA) 
        var trueAnomaly = eccentricToTrueAnomaly(e, eA) 
		heavenlyBodies[hB].trueAnomoly = trueAnomaly
		
	 //	console.log(hBName + " time = " +  heavenlyBodies[hB].time + "  delta time " + dt)		
	 // console.log(hBName + " eccentric anomaly " + E + " sin(f) " + sinf + " cos(f) " + cosf )
	 //	console.log(hBName + " mean anomaly " + mA + " eccentric anomaly " + eA ) 		
     // console.log (hBName + " trueAnomaly = " + trueAnomaly + "   true Anomaly  " + heavenlyBodies[hB].trueAnomoly + "  mean motion = " + n) ;
	 // console.log(hBName + " eccentricity " + e + " true anomaly " + f + " Eccentric anomaly " + eA + " Mean anomaly " + m0 + " mean motion " + n) 	 
	  }
	  updateTheDate() ;
	  
	};
	/*----------------------------------------------*

	function toggleOrbits() 
	{  // Step through a list of orbits and show or hide them via transparency.
	   var button = document.getElementById("orbits")
       var opacity = 0 ;
	   
	   solid = !solid;
		
		if (solid) {
		   button.value = "Orbits Off";	
		   opacity = 1 ;   
		}
		else {
			button.value = "Orbits On";
			opacity = 0 ;
		}

		 omat.setAttribute("transparency",opacity) ;
	   }
	}
	function toggleLabels() 
	{  // Step through a list of asteroid labels and show or hide them via transparency.
	
	   var button = document.getElementById("labels")
       var opacity = 0 ;
	   
	   solidLabels = !solidLabels;
		
		if (solidLabels) {
		   button.value = "Labels Off";

			button.value = "Labels On";
			opacity = 0 ;
		}
	   for (var hB in asteroidLabels) {

		 omat.setAttribute("transparency",opacity) ;
	   }
	}
//-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
	function traceOrbits()  
	{  // Generate line segments from points around the trajectory of the orbiting objects.
	   // Trace the orbits for the following array of objects.
	for (var hB in heavenlyBodies) {
	   var orbPos = [];
	   var j = 0;                // Initialize the orbit index, which will build the orbIndices list.
	   var orbitCoords = "";     // list of orbit coordinates
	   var orbIndices = "";      // Offsets into the list of orbit coordinates.
	   var i = 0.0 ;
	   while (i <= 6.28) {
	     orbPos = heavenlyBodies[hB].propagate(i) ;   // Earth.propagate(i) ;
         orbitCoords = orbitCoords + orbPos[0].toFixed(2)  + " " + orbPos[1].toFixed(2)  + " " + orbPos[2].toFixed(2)  + " " ;
		 orbIndices = orbIndices + j + " " ;
		//  i = i + 0.157 ;      // Advance to the next point around the orbit.
		 i = i + 0.0785
		 j = j + 1 ;          // Increment the orbit index.
        }
		orbIndices = orbIndices + -1 ;

		var s = document.createElement('Shape');            // Shape Node
		s.setAttribute("id", heavenlyBodies[hB].name + "Orbit");

		var app = document.createElement('Appearance');     // Appearance Node
		
		var omat = document.getElementById(heavenlyBodies[hB].name + 'Mat');
		var oMatC = omat.getAttribute("diffuseColor") ;
		
		var mat = document.createElement('Material');       // Material Node
           // mat.setAttribute("emissiveColor", 1 + " " + 0 + " " + 0.3);
		   mat.setAttribute("id", heavenlyBodies[hB].name + "OrbitMat");
		   mat.setAttribute("emissiveColor", oMatC);
		app.appendChild(mat);
		s.appendChild(app);
		
		var line = document.createElement('IndexedLineSet');
        line.setAttribute("coordIndex", orbIndices);
		var coords = document.createElement('Coordinate');
		coords.setAttribute("point", orbitCoords);
		
		line.appendChild(coords) ;
		
		s.appendChild(line);
		var ot = document.getElementById('theSun');
        ot.appendChild(s);
	 }
  };
```

## File: X3Dom/README.md
```markdown
# spacemission
The EarthToMoon_demo.html, LunarOrbit_withTexture.czml, and LunarProbeTrajectory_withBillboard.czml constitute the source code for this Cesium demonstration [http://daoneil.github.io/spacemission/Apps/EarthToMoon_Demo.html](http://daoneil.github.io/spacemission/Apps/EarthToMoon_Demo.html). Buttons enable selection various view-points. 
Right-click-and-drag to zoom in and out.
```

## File: X3Dom/WebMissionVisualizationTutorialSeries.html
```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<html>
<head>
<title>Web-based Space Mission Visualization</title>
</head>
<style>
div {
    margin-top: 30px;
    margin-left: 150px;
}
table, th, td {
   padding: 10px;
   text-align: center;
   border: 1px solid black;
}

</style>
<script>
 function showSimpleTrajectory() {
       document.getElementById("demoArea").innerHTML= "<object height='720' width='800' data='Trajectory_JSON.html' type='text/html'></object>" ;
   };
 function showHohmannTransfer() {
       document.getElementById("demoArea").innerHTML= '<object height="780" width="800" data="AHohmannTrajectory_JSON.html" type="text/html"></object>' ;
   };
 function showJSONConverter() {
       document.getElementById("demoArea").innerHTML= '<object height="700" width="900" data="Data_to_JSON_Converter6.html" type="text/html"></object>' ;
   };
 function showJSON_Reader() {
       document.getElementById("demoArea").innerHTML= '<object height="800" width="900" data="JSON_Trajectory_Reader_with_Model_appendix.html" type="text/html"></object>' ;
   };  
   
</script>

<body>
<div>
<H1>A Three Part Tutorial and a Vision for Creating<br> 
a Web-based Mission Visualization System</H1>
<table>
<tr><td>
<p>Part 1 of the tutorial series explains how to generate
<br>a trajectory data file with the General Mission
<br>Analysis Tool(GMAT) and to produce a simple 
<br>web-based mission visualization.</p></td>
<td><a href="20150918_WebVisualization_of_a_GMAT_GeneratedTrajectory_Part1.pdf">Part 1</a></td>
<td><button onclick="showSimpleTrajectory()">Demo 1</button></td><td id="demoArea" rowspan="5">Select a demonstration.</td></tr>

<tr><td>
<p>Part 2 of the tutorial series explains how to 
<br>apply a texture map to an X3D sphere and animate
<br>an X3D object to follow the GMAT generated trajectory.</p></td>
<td><a href="20150923_WebVisualization_of_a_GMAT_generatedTrajectory_Part2.pdf">Part 2</a></td>
<td><button onclick="showHohmannTransfer()">Demo 2</button></td></tr>

<tr><td>
<p>Part 3 of the tutorial series explains how to 
<br>write a JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) converter,
<br>import an X3D model, and use the HTML5 Filereader API.
<br>Before starting Demo 3, copy and paste the Input Data 
<br>into a text editor, save the file with a *.txt 
<br>extension, and upload it with the browse button Demo 3.</p></td>
<td><a href="20151102_WebVisualization_of_a_GMAT_generatedTrajectory_Part3.pdf">Part 3</a><p><a href="MolniyaOrbit.txt">Input Data</a></p></td>
<td><button onclick="showJSONConverter()">Demo 3</button></td></tr>

<tr><td>
<p>Before starting Demo 4, copy and paste the Output Data 
<br>into a text editor, save the a file with a *.json 
<br>extension and upload it with the Browse button on Demo 4.</p></td>
<td><a href="MolniyaOrbit.json">Output Data</a></p></td>
<td><button onclick="showJSON_Reader()()">Demo 4</button></td></tr>

<tr><td>
<p>A vision for a Web-based Mission Visualization System 
<br>(WMVS)involves provding tutorials and example source code
<br>to a community of developers and space mission designers. 
<br>This document presents a vision, use cases, desirable
<br>functions and features, and needed skills for a WMVS. </p></td>
<td colspan="2"><a href="20150611_WebBasedMissionVisualizationSystem.pdf">A Vision for a WMVS</a></p></td>
</table>
</div>
</body>
</html>
```

## File: X3Dom/x3dom.css
```css
/*
 * X3DOM JavaScript Library
 * http://www.x3dom.org
 *
 * (C)2009 Fraunhofer IGD, Darmstadt, Germany
 * Dual licensed under the MIT and GPL
 *
 * Based on code originally provided by
 * Philip Taylor: http://philip.html5.org
 */

body {
  background-color: white;
  font-family: Helvetica, sans-serif;
  font-size: 12px;
}

X3D, x3d {
  position:relative;    /* in order to be able to position stat-div within X3D */
  float:left;           /* float the element so it has the same size like the canvas */
  cursor:pointer;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  border: 1px solid #000;
}

object {
	margin: 0;
	padding: 0;
	border: none;
	z-index: 0;
  width:100%;
  height:100%;
  float:left;
}

X3D:hover, 
x3d:hover, 
.x3dom-canvas:hover {
  -webkit-user-select: none;
  -webkit-touch-callout: none;
}

.x3dom-canvas {
  border:none;
  cursor:pointer;
  cursor:-webkit-grab;
  cursor:grab;
  width:100%;
  height:100%;
  float:left;
}

.x3dom-canvas-mousedown {
  cursor:-webkit-grabbing;
  cursor:grabbing;
}

.x3dom-canvas:focus {
    outline:none; 
}
.x3dom-progress {
    margin: 0;
    padding: 6px 8px 0px 26px;
    left: 0px;
    top: 0px;
    position: absolute;
    color: #0f0;
    font-family: Helvetica, sans-serif;
    line-height:10px;
    font-size: 10px;
    min-width: 45px;
    min-height: 20px;
    border: 0px;
    background-position: 4px 4px;
    background-repeat: no-repeat;
    background-color: #333;
    background-color: rgba(51, 51, 51, 0.9);
    z-index: 100;
    background-image: url('data:image/gif;base64,');
}

.x3dom-progress.bar span {
  position: absolute;
  left: 0;
  top: 0;
  line-height: 20px;
  background-color: red;
}


.x3dom-statdiv {
    margin: 0;
    padding: 0;
    right: 10px;
    top: 10px;
    position: absolute;
    color: #0f0;
    font-family: Helvetica, sans-serif;
    line-height:10px;
    font-size: 10px;
    width: 75px;
    height: 70px;
    border: 0px;
}

#x3dom-state-canvas {
    margin: 2px;
    padding: 0;
    right: 0%;
    top: 0%;
    position: absolute;
}

#x3dom-state-viewer {
  position: absolute;
  margin: 2px;
  padding: 5px;
  width: 135px;
  top: 0%;
  right: 0%;
  opacity: 0.9;
  background-color: #323232;
  z-index: 1000;
  font-family: Arial, sans-serif;
  color: #C8C8C8;
  font-weight: bold;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  cursor: help;
}

.x3dom-states-head {
  display: block;
  font-size: 26px;
}

.x3dom-states-head2 {
  font-size: 10px;
}

.x3dom-states-list {
  float: left;
  width: 100%;
  border-top: 1px solid #C8C8C8;
  list-style: none;
  font-size: 9px;
  line-height: 16px;
  margin:0;
  padding: 0;
  padding-top: 2px;
}

.x3dom-states-item  {
  width: 100%;
  float: left;
}

.x3dom-states-item-title {
  float: left;
  margin-left: 2px;
}

.x3dom-states-item-value {
  float: right;
  margin-right: 2px;
}

.x3dom-touch-marker {
	display: inline;
    padding: 5px;
	border-radius: 10px;
    position: absolute;
    font-family: Helvetica, sans-serif;
    line-height:10px;
    font-size: 10px;
    color: darkorange;
    background: cornsilk;
    opacity: 0.6;
    border: 2px solid orange;
	z-index: 200;
}

.x3dom-logContainer {
    border: 2px solid olivedrab;
    height: 200px;
    padding: 4px;
    overflow: auto;
    white-space: pre-wrap;
    font-family: sans-serif;
    font-size: x-small;
    color: #00ff00;
    background-color: black;
    margin-right: 10px;
}

.x3dom-nox3d {
    font-family: Helvetica, sans-serif;
    font-size: 14px;
    background-color: #eb7a7a;
    padding: 1em;
    opacity: 0.75;
}

.x3dom-nox3d p { 
    color: #fff;
    font-size: 14px;
}

.x3dom-nox3d a { 
    color: #fff;
    font-size: 14px;
}


/* self-clearing floats */
.group:after {
  content: "."; 
  display: block; 
  height: 0; 
  clear: both; 
  visibility: hidden;
}
```

## File: index.html
```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
<title>Mission Visualization</title>
<style>
body {
  background-color:#F8F8F8;
}
#banner {
  display: table-cell;
  background-color: SlateBlue;
  padding: 10px;
  vertical-align: middle;
}
h2 {
  color: white;
  text-align: center;

}
</style>
</head>
<body>
<div id="banner">
  <h2>Web-based Space Mission Visualization</h2>
</div>


<p>Contents of the Web-based Space Mission Visualization (WSMV)
repository include Orrery demonstration web-apps and tutorials for depicting
orbital trajectories.</p>
  <h4><a href="https://github.com/nasa/mission-viz">Repository https://github.com/nasa/mission-viz</a></h4>

<h4>Web-Apps</h4>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://nasa.github.io/mission-viz/OntologyDrivenOrrery/An_Orrery_in_ThreeJS.html">Ontology-based Orrery</a> <span>Markup Language (HTML) page with an embedded 3D model of the solar system with Keplerian orbital parameters expressed as a orbit
class from a Space Situational Awareness Ontology. The model was created with
the X3DOM JavaScript code library.</span> </li>
<li><a href="https://nasa.github.io/mission-viz/RMarkdown/ontology_based_orrery_generated_from_R_code.html">Orrery and orbital parameters table</a> <span> R code generated HTML page with an embedded 3D modelof the solar system with a table of planetary orbital parameters. </span></li>
<li><a href="https://nasa.github.io/mission-viz/X3Dom/InnerSolarSystem.html">Orrery
with Potentially Hazardous Asteroids</a> <span> - An HTML page with an embedded
interactive animated 3D model of the inner planets of the solar system and 50
potentially hazardous asteroids. The model was created with the X3DOM
JavaScript code library. Original JavaScript code implements an orbital
propagator described in “Orbital Mechanics, Theory and Applications by Tom
Logsdon.<span></li>
<li><a href="https://nasa.github.io/mission-viz/X3Dom/20160129_Earth_MoonMission_X3D.html">Earth
Moon Mission Visualization</a> <span>- An HTML page with an interactive 3D animated
model a spacecraft moving from an Earth orbit to a Lunar orbit. The model was
produced with the X3DOM JavaScript code library.</span></li>
</ul>
<p></p>

<h4>Tutorials</h4>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://nasa.github.io/mission-viz/RMarkdown/Elliptical_Orbit_Design.html">How
to design a 3D elliptical orbit</a><span> - An
R code generated HTML page with interactive 3D models of elliptical orbits.
This web-app explains how to transform a 2D ellipse into a 3D orbit and how to
implement an orbital propagator. </span></li>
<li><a
href="https://nasa.github.io/mission-viz/X3Dom/WebMissionVisualizationTutorialSeries.html">Web-based
Space Mission Visualization Tutorial Series</a> <span> - An HTML web page that provide links to tutorials in
Portable Data Files (PDF) and the interactive demonstrations described in items
d, e, f, and g on this list. </span></li>

<li><a href="https://nasa.github.io/mission-viz/OntologyDrivenOrrery/20160830_Importing_the_SpaceSituationalAwarenessOntology_and_Exporting_JSONLD.pdf">Importing data into an ontology and exporting JSON-LD</a> <span>- A presentation that
     explains how to import data from Excel into an ontology within Protégé</span></li>
<li><a href="https://nasa.github.io/mission-viz/RMarkdown/20180515_Generating_an_HTMLTable_and_3D_Plot_with_R_from_JSONLD.pdf">Generate
     a table and 3D plot using R</a></li>
 <li><a href="https://nasa.github.io/mission-viz/X3Dom/20150611_WebBasedMissionVisualizationSystem.pdf">A
     vision for a community developed web-based orrery</a></li>
</ul>

<p></p>

<h4>Ontology</h4>
<ul>
<li><a href= "https://github.com/nasa/mission-viz/blob/main/OntologyDrivenOrrery/SSAO_Rovetto.owl">Space Situational Awareness Ontology developed by Robert Rovetto</a>
<li><a href="https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20210000030/downloads/NASA_TM_20210000030.pdf">An Ontology-Based Virtual Orrery</a>

</ul>

</body>
</html>
```

## File: README.md
```markdown
# mission-viz
Web-based Space Mission Visualization software

### Web-apps:
- [An Orrery implemented in ThreeJS](https://nasa.github.io/mission-viz/OntologyDrivenOrrery/An_Orrery_in_ThreeJS.html)
- [An Orrery implmented in R](https://nasa.github.io/mission-viz/RMarkdown/ontology_based_orrery_generated_from_R_code.html)
- [An Orrery with Potentially Hazardous Asteroids](https://nasa.github.io/mission-viz/X3Dom/InnerSolarSystem.html)
- [An Earth Moon mission visualization](https://nasa.github.io/mission-viz/X3Dom/20160129_Earth_MoonMission_X3D.html)

### Tutorials
- [How to design a 3D elliptical orbit](https://nasa.github.io/mission-viz/RMarkdown/Elliptical_Orbit_Design.html)
- [Web-based Space Mission Visualization Tutorial Series](https://nasa.github.io/mission-viz/X3Dom/WebMissionVisualizationTutorialSeries.html)
- [Importing data into an ontology and exporting JSON-LD](https://nasa.github.io/mission-viz/OntologyDrivenOrrery/20160830_Importing_the_SpaceSituationalAwarenessOntology_and_Exporting_JSONLD.pdf)
- [Generate a table and 3D plot using R](https://nasa.github.io/mission-viz/RMarkdown/20180515_Generating_an_HTMLTable_and_3D_Plot_with_R_from_JSONLD.pdf)
- [A vision for a communicty developed web-based orrery](https://nasa.github.io/mission-viz/X3Dom/20150611_WebBasedMissionVisualizationSystem.pdf)
```
